info.name: KoboMarket API
info.description:
Multi-vendor marketplace with wallets, a double-entry ledger and escrow. Money is integer kobo (NGN 1 = 100 kobo).

1. Start the stack and load demo data: `docker compose up -d` then `docker compose exec api npm run seed`.
2. Run **Demo flow** top to bottom (or with the Runner): each request saves the ids the next one needs.
3. **All endpoints** has every operation from /api-docs.json, grouped like Swagger. They use {{accessToken}}, set by the last login.

Demo password for every seeded account: KoboMarket#2026

exec: // Money endpoints need an Idempotency-Key. A fresh one is added for every send;
// set the collection variable fixedIdempotencyKey to reuse one (replay or 409 demo).
// Today in Lagos time (UTC+1), for the revenue report.

item.name: 1. Demo flow
item.description: Fund → checkout → ship → confirm → payout, then a dispute with a partial refund, then the admin reports.

item.name: Browse Ada's products (pick one without variants)
Pay on the mock checkout (sends the webhook twice)
Add the product to the cart

request.description: Without the worker running, a second run of the flow gets 409 PAYOUT_PENDING until the first payout is processed.

item.name: Dispute: admin resolves with a partial refund (NGN 2,000)

request.description: Notifications are created by the worker; without it running this list may be empty.

item.name: GET /health  ·  Liveness: the process is up
GET /health/ready  ·  Readiness: PostgreSQL and MongoDB are reachable
GET /admin/users  ·  List and search users, newest first
PATCH /admin/users/{id}/freeze  ·  Freeze a user (no orders, no withdrawals)

request.description: Sets the user FROZEN in MongoDB and their wallet FROZEN in PostgreSQL, so the ledger itself refuses their debits. Refunds can still arrive. Safe to repeat.

item.name: GET /admin/wallets/{id}/ledger  ·  Any wallet (user or system account) and its full ledger history
GET /admin/transactions  ·  All ledger transactions with their entries, newest first
PATCH /admin/settings/commission  ·  Set the commission rate for future checkouts

request.description: Basis points (500 = 5%), 0 to 5000. Existing sub-orders keep the rate snapshotted at checkout.

item.name: GET /admin/vendors  ·  List applications, oldest first (cursor pagination)
PATCH /admin/vendors/{id}/approve  ·  Approve a pending application and grant the vendor role (safe to repeat)
PATCH /admin/vendors/{id}/reject  ·  Reject a pending application with a reason
GET /admin/reports/revenue  ·  Platform revenue per day for a date range (Lagos days)
GET /admin/reports/top-vendors  ·  Top 10 vendors by completed sales this month (net of partial refunds)
GET /admin/reports/escrow  ·  Money currently held in escrow, beside the unfinished sub-orders behind it
GET /admin/reports/reconciliation  ·  Wallets whose cached balance differs from their ledger sum (should be empty)
POST /auth/register  ·  Register with email and password

request.description: Creates an unverified buyer, opens their wallet in PostgreSQL and emails a one-time verification token (logged to the console). If the wallet cannot be opened the user is still created with walletStatus PENDING and a job retries.

item.name: POST /auth/verify-email  ·  Verify email with the emailed token (24 h, single use)
POST /auth/login  ·  Log in; returns a 15-minute access token and a 7-day refresh token

request.description: Max 5 attempts per email + IP per 15 minutes. A successful login resets the count.
Returns a new access + refresh token pair; the presented token is retired. Presenting a token that was already rotated is treated as theft and signs the user out of every session.

item.name: POST /auth/logout  ·  Sign out this device (revokes its refresh token chain)
POST /auth/forgot-password  ·  Email a password reset token (30 min)

request.description: Always returns 200 so it cannot be used to discover accounts.

item.name: POST /auth/reset-password  ·  Set a new password with the reset token; signs out every session

request.description: Email, password, roles and status cannot be changed here; any other field is a 422. Passwords change through forgot/reset password.

item.name: GET /cart  ·  Your cart, checked against live products

request.description: Each line shows the live unit price and stock and lists its problems: PRICE_CHANGED (live price differs from when it was added), INSUFFICIENT_STOCK, UNAVAILABLE (deleted, inactive or variant removed), OWN_PRODUCT. `ready` is true only when no line has a problem. subtotalKobo is at live prices.

item.name: POST /cart/items  ·  Add an item (adds to the qty if it is already in the cart)
POST /sub-orders/{id}/disputes  ·  Open a dispute on your shipped sub-order (buyer)

request.description: The sub-order becomes DISPUTED and its escrow is frozen (auto-complete skips it) until an admin resolves the dispute. Confirming delivery releases the money straight away, so disputes are opened before confirming.

item.name: PATCH /disputes/{id}/respond  ·  Reply to a dispute on your sub-order, with your own evidence (vendor, once)
GET /disputes/mine  ·  Disputes where you are the buyer or the vendor
GET /disputes/{id}  ·  One dispute with both sides' evidence (admin)

request.description: FULL_REFUND: the whole sub-order back to the buyer (sub-order REFUNDED). PARTIAL_REFUND: refundKobo to the buyer, the rest to the vendor minus commission on that rest only (sub-order COMPLETED). REJECTED: released to the vendor as a normal completion. The admin's id and the note are recorded.

item.name: GET /notifications  ·  Your notifications, newest first (cursor pagination)

request.description: Types: ORDER_PLACED, NEW_ORDER, ORDER_CANCELLED, ORDER_SHIPPED, FUNDS_RELEASED, DISPUTE_OPENED, DISPUTE_RESOLVED, PAYOUT_SUCCEEDED, PAYOUT_FAILED. The response also carries unreadCount.

item.name: GET /notifications/unread-count  ·  How many of your notifications are unread
PATCH /notifications/{id}/read  ·  Mark one notification read (safe to repeat)
PATCH /notifications/read-all  ·  Mark all your notifications read

request.description: Re-checks every cart line against live products (a changed price, missing stock or removed product stops checkout with 409 CART_NOT_READY; prices in the cart are updated so the buyer can check out again). Then reserves stock, and in one PostgreSQL transaction moves the total from the wallet to escrow and creates one order with one PAID sub-order per vendor. Idempotent: the same Idempotency-Key returns the same order.

item.name: GET /orders  ·  Your orders, newest first (cursor pagination)

request.description: status is derived from the sub-orders (shared status, or IN_PROGRESS).

item.name: POST /orders/{id}/cancel  ·  Cancel an order before anything ships (refunds escrow, restocks)

request.description: All or nothing; refused if any sub-order is no longer PAID.
Starts the escrow timeout (escrow_timeout_hours, default 72) for auto-complete.

item.name: PATCH /sub-orders/{id}/confirm  ·  Confirm delivery (buyer); releases escrow to the vendor

request.description: SHIPPED to DELIVERED to COMPLETED in one transaction. Escrow is split: the vendor gets the subtotal minus commission (rate snapshotted at checkout, rounded down), PLATFORM_REVENUE gets the commission.

item.name: GET /vendors/me/sub-orders  ·  Your store's sub-orders, newest first (vendor)
POST /payouts  ·  Request a payout to your bank account (vendor)

request.description: The amount leaves your wallet at once into payout clearing; a background job sends the transfer within about 30 seconds. On success the payout is SUCCESS; on failure the money comes back to your wallet and it is FAILED. Only one PENDING payout at a time. Minimum is the payout_min_kobo setting (default 100000 kobo = NGN 1,000). With the mock provider, a bank account number ending in 0000 always fails (for demos and tests).

item.name: GET /products  ·  Browse and search the catalogue (cursor pagination)

request.description: Only active, non-deleted products. `q` narrows by full-text search on name, tags and description; results are ordered by `sort` (no relevance order, because a relevance score cannot be used as a cursor). Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` with the same `sort` to get the next page.

item.name: POST /products  ·  Create a product (vendor with an approved store)
GET /products/{slug}  ·  One product by slug (404 if inactive or deleted)

request.description: A product with variants takes price and stock per variant; sending a top-level priceKobo or stock is refused. Sending `variants: []` removes them and then needs priceKobo and stock. Stock is set to the number sent.

item.name: POST /products/{id}/reviews  ·  Review a product you received (buyer)

request.description: Only buyers with a COMPLETED order containing the product may review it, once per product. The product's rating (avg, count) updates at once.

item.name: GET /vendors/me/products  ·  Your own catalogue, inactive products included
POST /vendors/apply  ·  Apply to become a vendor (one store per user)

request.description: Creates a PENDING application. After a rejection the same user may apply again, which puts the application back to PENDING. Frozen users are refused.

item.name: GET /vendors/me  ·  The caller's own application, with status and masked bank details
GET /vendors/{id}  ·  Public store profile (approved stores only, no bank details)
GET /wallet/transactions  ·  Your wallet's ledger entries, newest first (cursor pagination)

request.description: Returns the provider's checkout URL. The wallet is credited only when the provider's signed webhook arrives and the payment is re-verified with the provider. Idempotent: the same Idempotency-Key and body return the same funding; a different body with the same key is a 409.

item.name: POST /webhooks/paystack  ·  Paystack webhook (called by Paystack, not by clients)

request.description: The raw body must carry a valid x-paystack-signature (HMAC-SHA512 with the secret key). charge.success credits the matching funding exactly once, after re-verifying the amount with Paystack. Redelivered events are acknowledged and ignored.

item.name: GET /mock-paystack/checkout/{reference}  ·  What a mock payment is for (only when PAYMENT_PROVIDER=mock)
POST /mock-paystack/checkout/{reference}/pay  ·  Pay a funding on the mock provider (only when PAYMENT_PROVIDER=mock)

request.description: Marks the payment successful and sends the signed charge.success webhook twice.
